newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritian group investing in Mozambican sugar.
newsitem.headline: Mauritian group investing in Mozambican sugar.

text.p: A Mauritian consortium intends to invest up to 1.54 billion rupees ($75 million) in two sugar mills in Mozambique, namely Marromeu and Luabo, one of the companies in the consortium said on Tuesday.
Hector Espitalier Noel, chief executive of the Espitalier Noel Group (ENG), said the consortium included ENG, Mon Loisir Group (MLG) and Flacq United Estates Ltd (FUEL) Group.
The consortium will provide some of the money but most of it will come from foreign funds, he said. "A fine tuned feasibility study will fix the shareholding structure," he added.

"Technical studies are in process so as to determine the very exact nature of the soil that could be favourable to sugar cane cultivation and also to take note of the existing factories' real potential to produce sugar," he said.
The private-sector consortium will also develop farming on 75,000 hectares (190,000 acres), he added.
"The Mozambican project does not constitute a threat to the Mauritian sugar industry as the consortium is deeply involved in the local sugar sector," he said.
